behavior: Opt-in persistent authenticated second SEQPACKET channel. Every later opening obtains a fresh live child subject and prepaid held data loan from the original funded owner. SQL4 atomically commits intent and unique session association before a typed worker-scoped permission; initial startup remains single-use.

history.meaning: Controlled protocol and kernel transport; not financing proof.
Initial real SQL/transport/C1-C3.A compatibility acceptance before lifecycle corrections.
Reproduced false repeated uncertainty, reinstallation after close, invalid local input poisoning and idle timeout poisoning.
Foreign task could poll before funding ownership was checked.
Corrected lifecycle and ownership plus SQL4 constraints and compatibility; all eight production files equal final acceptance.
Strengthened the existing parallel test: barrier inside driver call and same backend before/after connection barrier. Only test fixture changed, root reviewed and full final suite includes it.

invariants: Launch broker requires explicit first_sql_grant and rejects inherited reserved descriptors; protocols2/3 keep meaning.
Only the original approved startup issuer installs the client; installation and close are monotonic; startup_spent never resets.
Actual SCM sender, original parent/child kernel view and bounded exact schemas/nonce/sequence/destination protect each exchange; all received rights are closed on refusal.
Per-request grant is captured on actual requesting PID/Thread/task; no network or SQL under gate.guard and no exchange lock across driver.
Parent retains exact original channel and checks funded PID/Thread/task/scope/raw/target before any IPC; fresh request subjects expire after each serve.
One held prepared data unit is borrowed for each request; charge can claim only one intent on its exact original channel and subject.
SQL4 maps intent to unique session_id, with exactly one matching startup/follow-up FK, in the same confirmed transaction; actual RETURNING data verified.
Startup funding is mapped in broker mode; legacy v3 historical startups are not silently remapped.
Idle is distinct from EOF; invalid local input/busy exchange is known refusal, while sent unknown requests fail terminal with stable IDs.
Broker failure detaches before closing; later local refusals do not manufacture more registration uncertainty.
Failures and client/channel closure retain the original whole lease. Claim without row after rollback is retained debt, not reusable authority.
limits: No production Bridge/provider activation, root genesis/first control TCP funding, full inventory, independently funded custody or global M1/M2/M3 acceptance.
Runtime cooperation boundary, not a sandbox against arbitrary trusted Python/raw SQL or credential changes.
A pre-attach descendant may inherit and steal a descriptor for denial of service; SCM prevents impersonation, and after attach fork closes the inherited channel.
IPC is synchronous and deadline-bounded; async integration must use an owner worker that creates/keeps its own supervisor and funding, not transfer existing objects to an executor.

Parent idle timeout preserves channel; client timeout after send is terminal. Slow dispatch or cancellation can leave a paid orphan; pre-charge HUP polling is best-effort, never absence or refund proof.
Busy exchange timeout refuses only the local unsent request. No automatic request retry, resynchronization or data-credit refund.
SQL4 owner migration is required before current journal APIs; no runtime DDL fallback. Runtime ACL is append-only; database owner remains trusted for migration/fixture provisioning.
Logical journal quota bounds metadata records and one association per intent, not physical byte or global session coverage.
Twenty sequential openings and five concurrent SQL workers in one child are not twenty/five agents or distributed-network capacity.
All ten original gates and SDK/UI configuration remain open.
